Christine Drazan

Republican, Libertarian candidate for Governor, Oregon · Challenger

Oregon state senator (R-Canby); former Oregon House Republican leader

Christine Drazan is a Republican state senator from Canby who grew up in Klamath Falls. She was the 2022 Republican nominee for governor and won the 2026 Republican primary on May 19, 2026, with about 41% of the vote. The Libertarian Party also nominated her, and she is running against Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek in a rematch of 2022.

Where Drazan stands

Affordability and utility costs
Promises to cut taxes. Criticizes taxes approved during Gov. Kotek's first term, naming taxes on nicotine pouches, insurance, paychecks, cars and paddleboards. Says she opposes a sales tax.
Economy and jobs
Promises to work for repeal of Oregon's estate tax, which starts at $1 million. When businesses consider leaving, says she would ask what they need to stay and lower the barriers.
Economy and jobs
Supports tax-break programs for companies as long as they support the community and a wide range of industries. Has announced plans to cut taxes and regulations in the Portland area.
Data centers
In the Medford debate, said she would push for a moratorium on new data centers, as Gov. Kotek also did.
Health care and food assistance
Supports SNAP food assistance and says her family relied on food stamps when she was a child. Criticizes the state's error rate in approving benefits and says the state should communicate better so recipients can stay eligible.
K-12 education
Says the state's current approach to struggling schools, with small step-by-step commitments to change, has not worked. Joined parents calling on Portland and Salem-Keizer district leaders to protect neighborhood schools.
Housing and homelessness
Has spoken against needle exchanges near schools in Multnomah County.
Federal administration
Says she would govern independently of national politics, which she says has its own weather system she has never been dragged into. Argues a governor and a legislature from different parties can work together.
Public safety
Has called for Portland City Councilor Mitch Green to resign over his comments about eliminating police, and criticizes Gov. Kotek for staying silent on them.

Background

  • Oregon State Senator (appointed October 2025 to the seat vacated by Sen. Daniel Bonham)
  • Oregon House Republican Leader (2019–2021; again in 2025)
  • Member, Oregon House of Representatives (elected 2018; resigned in 2021 to run for governor; returned in 2025)
  • Republican nominee for Oregon governor, 2022
  • Former legislative aide and chief of staff to Oregon House Speaker Mark Simmons (1990s)
  • Grew up in Klamath Falls
